chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṣabbāḥ al-Azraq, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), “A man from the Mukhtāriyya met me and claimed that Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya is an Imam.” So Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) became angry, then said, “Why did you not say something to him?” He said: I replied, “No, by Allah, I did not know what to say.”

He said, “Why did you not say to him: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) gave the bequest to ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn. Then when ʿAlī (عليه السلام) passed away, he bequeathed to al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn. If he had tried to turn it away from them both, they would have said to him, ‘We are two legatees just like you,’ and he would not have done that.”

And al-Ḥasan bequeathed to al-Ḥusayn, and if he had tried to turn it away from him, he would have said, ‘I am a legatee like you, from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) and from my father,’ and he would not have done that.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “And those related by blood are nearer to one another.”
It is about us and about our sons.

key_terms.أَبْنَائِنَا: our sons, referring to the descendants of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.أَوْصَى: he bequeathed or designated by testamentary instruction
key_terms.أَوْلَى: more entitled, having greater priority or claim
key_terms.أُولُوا الْأَرْحَامِ: blood relatives or kin possessing family ties
key_terms.إِمَامٌ: the divinely designated leader whose authority is being discussed
key_terms.الْمُخْتَارِيَّةِ: the group associated with al-Mukhtār, mentioned here for a disputed claim about the Imam

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith use the Quran to prove the succession of the Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the ordered succession of authority among the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام through explicit bequest, beginning from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and continuing through Imam ʿAlī, Imam al-Ḥasan, and Imam al-Ḥusayn عليهم السلام. It also applies the Quranic principle of kinship priority to the line of the Imams, showing that this authority remains within them and their descendants.
